editorial:
Imagine booking a quiet countryside getaway to fix your marriage, only to find the house itself seems to have other plans. Kevin Bacon plays a troubled husband with a dark past, while Amanda Seyfried plays his much younger wife, and their young daughter rounds out the family. The film starts like a cozy retreat, then slowly turns into a tense, mind-bending nightmare where hallways stretch, time feels off, and secrets bubble up. It has a slow-burn mood that keeps you uneasy rather than throwing jump scares every minute.

The acting is strong, especially Bacon, who sells the fear and guilt without overdoing it. The house design is clever, and the pacing builds nicely, though some viewers may find the middle a bit slow. The biggest downside is that the mystery can feel confusing before it clicks. If you enjoy psychological horror with a family drama core, this is a solid pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the house traps Kevin Bacon's character as punishment for his past crime. He realizes the home feeds on guilt and wants him to stay forever. To save his wife and daughter, he makes them leave without him and accepts his fate inside the house. The twist is that the retreat was never a real vacation; it was a supernatural trap designed to confront his sins. He stays behind so his family can escape, ending the nightmare for them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological horror with family drama and a creepy house mystery.
